name: 03-second-look
description: The parts of the interface every card shares, each one pressed so you see what it does.

steps.title: The second look
steps.caption: The second look. Five buttons, pressed.
Every card is built the same way, so learning one teaches you all of them.
Mode decides how much you see. Expert adds controls, each marked with a small slider.
Developer shows the rest, so you can tell a setting is there before you need it.
Back to user: the same device, with only what running it takes.
Now the buttons in the corner. Every card has them, and each does something you can watch.
A child module is a tab inside its parent, and it carries the same five.
{ } shows this card as JSON: the state document a preset holds, with a copy button and a link to its diagnostics.
Save it as a preset, or open the diagnostics and paste them into an issue, and the report carries what someone would have to ask you for.
⏻ turns a module off. The layer stops and the lights hold their last frame.
On again, and it picks up where it was.
✎ swaps the effect inside this layer for another type. Same slot in the pipeline.
Swap it back. Nothing else in the tree noticed.
🗑 deletes a module. These two appear only where a module is yours to change.
And add one back, because a layer is a module like any other.
With its effect, and the lights are running again.
The same pattern everywhere: Layouts, and its Grid inside.
Grid: the layout's own card, reached the same way.
Every control applies on the next frame. No save button, no reboot: I type two hundred and fifty six and the grid is already that wide.
And the height to match. Sixty five thousand lights, resized while the effect keeps running: the lights answer while you are still typing.
